title: The Doctrine of the Word
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Nature of Divine Revelation
subpoints: Revelation is God's initiative to unveil His character and will
It is an encounter with God, not merely the provision of information
Revelation serves a redemptive or damning purpose depending on the response

outline.title: The Historical Accuracy of Scripture
subpoints: The Bible claims to be historically accurate, not just a vehicle for theological truth
Critique of Neo-Orthodoxy (Barth, Bultmann) which separated history from revelation
The events described in Scripture actually happened as recorded

outline.title: Revelation Through Covenant
subpoints: God reveals Himself through covenants rather than abstract lectures
The Westminster Confession (WCF 7.1) affirms that God's condescension is expressed by way of covenant
Covenants define God's promises and the responsibilities of His people

outline.title: The Progression of the Covenant of Redemption
subpoints: The seed promise in Genesis 3:15 initiates the redemptive history
The lineage moves from the seed to the Shemites, then to Abraham, Israel, Judah, and the family of Jesse
The ultimate fulfillment is found in the Lord Jesus Christ, who brings the gospel to the whole world

summary:
This lesson, part of the Foundations series, explores the doctrine of the Word, also known as bibliology. The primary focus is on the nature of divine revelation, defined as God's voluntary unveiling of His character, purpose, and will to creation. It is emphasized that revelation is an initiative of God, undertaken out of mercy and grace, rather than a discovery made by humanity. The sermon distinguishes between general revelation, seen in creation, and special revelation, found in Scripture, noting that while both disclose God, they carry redemptive or damning implications based on human response.

A significant portion of the teaching addresses the historical reliability of the Bible. The speaker critiques the Neo-Orthodox movement, which argued that the historical accuracy of biblical events was secondary to their theological significance. In contrast, the sermon asserts that the Bible presents itself as a historically accurate account of events that actually occurred, maintaining that the truth of the Gospel is inextricably linked to its historical reality.

The lesson further examines how God reveals Himself through covenants. Citing the Westminster Confession of Faith, it explains that the vast distance between God and humanity is bridged by God's voluntary condescension, expressed through covenantal relationships. The sermon traces the progression of these covenants, from the covenant of works with Adam to the covenant of redemption, highlighting the seed promise in Genesis 3:15 as the foundational thread that leads through the lineages of Shem, Abraham, Israel, and Judah to the ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
